html:
The great earthquake that struck San Francisco and the coast of northern California early on 18 April 1906, and the fires that followed. It destroyed most of the city.

The San Andreas Fault slipped along a stretch of more than 400 kilometres, with a magnitude of about 7.9. The fires did more damage than the shaking. Broken gas lines started them and broken water mains left firemen without water. Some fires were set by owners whose insurance covered fire but not quakes, and soldiers dynamiting buildings to make firebreaks started others. The city burned for three days.

About 3,000 people died, though officials at first claimed far fewer. More than half the population lost their homes.

The fire also burned the city's birth records. Many Chinese residents then claimed to have been born there, which made them citizens and let them bring in relatives, called "paper sons", despite the Chinese Exclusion Act.

The city rebuilt quickly and showed itself off at a world's fair in 1915 marking the opening of the Panama Canal.
sum: The great earthquake that struck San Francisco and the coast of northern California early on 18 April 1906, and the fires that followed. It destroyed most of the city.
